system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Overall assessment:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced". It combines (a) a tight general limitation regime, (b) an attempt to pull every claim type – fundamental, tax, IP, specific indemnities – inside that regime, (c) a blanket data-room/public-register disclosure, and (d) a knowledge exclusion. Read together, these largely neutralise the warranty protection, while the known deal risks (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, the privacy incident) are either pushed to post-completion or left with the Buyer. The Disclosure Letter is actually more candid than the Seller Update – it concedes most of the gaps – so we should use it against the Update.

---

## A. Limitation architecture – the structural problems

**1. Fundamental/title warranties folded into general caps (Seller Update "Fundamental / Title")**
Unacceptable. Title and capacity warranties go to whether the Buyer gets what it is paying for. Market position: 100% of the price as cap, 6–7 year (or statutory limitation) claim period, not subject to de minimis/basket, not qualified by disclosure. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

**2. "All limitations apply to all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.3 / 12.8 / 13 / 20.5)**
This single drafting device is the most damaging item in the package. It would sweep specific indemnities, the tax indemnity, leakage/price-adjustment claims, and restraint claims into the 20%/18-month/basket regime, and the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language would then try to shut everything else out. Required carve-outs from caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance:
- fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment or wilful default (can't effectively be excluded anyway, but say so);
- fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances);
- tax warranties and tax indemnity (separate cap – 100% – and 7 years, reflecting ATO amendment periods);
- all specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark);
- completion accounts / debt-free-cash-free adjustment and leakage;
- claims under the Australian Consumer Law – we should not accept non-reliance drafting purporting to exclude s 18 misleading-or-deceptive-conduct claims (it is ineffective and signals intent);
- equitable relief / specific performance of Completion and restraint covenants.

**3. Cap (cl 12.1) – 20% / AUD 4.8m**
Low end for this profile. Given concentrated customer risk (Bluefen ~30% of revenue), an unresolved IP title issue and an open privacy incident, we should open at 50% with a tiered structure (e.g. 100% fundamental/tax; 40–50% IP, data/privacy, key contracts; 25–30% other general). If the Seller holds at 20%, price it: retention/escrow or W&I insurance with the Seller bearing a share of the premium.

**4. Thresholds (cl 12.2)**
The basket as drafted is a true deductible ("only the excess"). Push for a tipping basket (first dollar recoverable once AUD 250,000 is exceeded). De minimis AUD 25,000 is tolerable but require aggregation of claims arising from the same or related facts, so a series of related breaches is not sliced under the threshold. Thresholds should not apply to indemnities, tax or fundamental claims.

**5. Time limits (cl 12.3/13) – 18 months**
Acceptable for general commercial warranties *only* if tax (7 years), fundamental (6+ years), IP/privacy (at least 3 years) and indemnities (survival until limitation period) are carved out. Also require that a claim notified in time survives if proceedings are commenced within, say, 9–12 months thereafter.

**6. Disclosure standard (Schedule 7; DL [1.1]–[1.2])**
Reject general disclosure of "the data room" and "publicly searchable corporate records". Require: matters *fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect*; public-record disclosure limited to listed searches (ASIC, PPSR, court, IP Australia) on a specified date; no disclosure against fundamental warranties or indemnities. Note the Seller's own DL [11] says the Buyer "must evaluate the disclosed facts" – which is exactly why a bare data-room reference is not fair disclosure.

**7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)**
Delete. "Discoverable from the data room or public records" is a constructive-knowledge standard that would gut the warranties and double-counts with the general disclosure. If a compromise is needed: actual knowledge of 2–3 named Wattlebridge individuals, of a matter *and* that it constituted a breach, and never applying to fundamental warranties, tax or indemnities.

---

## B. Specific deal risks – conditions, price mechanics and indemnities

**8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3; DL [2]) – ~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue**
The Update says "addressed"; the Disclosure Letter says no final consent exists and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. The consent must be a true condition precedent: written, unconditional (or all 11.3 conditions satisfied and evidenced), in a form satisfied by the Buyer acting reasonably, and not waivable by the Seller. "Reasonable endeavours" to deliver is too weak – at least "all reasonable endeavours" with Buyer involvement in the approach. Consider commercial protection if Bluefen imposes conditions (price reduction, deferred consideration tied to Bluefen retention, or a termination right). Do not accept this as a post-completion undertaking.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7; DL [3]) – ~AUD 3.2m**
Fundamentally inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal. A release "following Completion" means the Buyer owns a company in change-of-control default (cl 8.1) with security on foot. Require at Completion: payout letter, repayment from the purchase price via the funds flow, executed deed of release, PPSR discharge (or undertaking to discharge within 2 business days with escrow), and a specific indemnity for any shortfall, break costs and residual encumbrance. Treat any unpaid balance as Debt in the price adjustment.

**10. Completion bonuses (DD-005; funds flow) – AUD 420,000 plus on-costs**
"A matter for the Seller" is only true if the Seller actually bears them. Because the Company is the employer, the economic burden lands on the Buyer unless deducted. Require: gross amount plus superannuation and NSW payroll tax (budget ~AUD 480–500k all-in) treated as Debt / transaction cost and deducted from the price or paid by the Seller before Completion; itemised in the funds flow; specific indemnity for any claim by employees; confirmation of the "continued employment" trigger so the Buyer is not exposed if staff later leave.

**11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL [4]) – AUD 180,000 unpaid; IP does not transfer until paid**
An indemnity capped at the SOW3 payment covers the wrong risk. The real exposure is that the Company does not own the SOW3 Project Materials, which may be embedded in its product. Require: payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay as a condition precedent (or deliverable at Completion); independent evidence of payment; unqualified IP ownership warranty; specific indemnity covering loss of title, infringement and remediation costs, not merely the AUD 180,000. Fix the AUD 180,000 as Debt if unpaid.

**12. Data export incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL [6]) – ~1,240 personal records**
The Seller's "preliminary / not material" is a characterisation, not a fact; the Disclosure Letter admits scope and access are unknown. Under the Privacy Act Notifiable Data Breaches scheme the Company had to assess within 30 days and may need to notify the OAIC and individuals; the post-2022/2024 penalty and enforcement regime is materially harsher (and a direct right of action is now in play). Require: completion of the assessment and provision of findings pre-Completion; notification where required; specific uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity for regulator action, notification costs, third-party and customer claims (check whether Bluefen's or other customer data is involved – that interacts with issue 8); ensure the disclosure does not qualify the data-protection warranties or the indemnity.

**13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – 3 × AUD 110,000**
Splitting across two data-room documents warrants scrutiny. Ask: are they committed or terminable; when were/are they signed; are they accrued in the Accounts/working capital; are they prepayments benefiting the Buyer or sunk costs? If not reflected in working capital or if entered between signing and Completion, treat as leakage/Debt or require Buyer consent under the pre-Completion conduct covenants. "Ordinary course" is asserted, not evidenced.

**14. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"**
Not agreed. Tax: separate warranties, a full tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, 100% cap, 7 years, no basket), and pre-Completion tax returns/ATO correspondence conduct provisions. IP: higher cap and longer period, and in light of Ironquay, no reliance on general disclosure.

**15. Title to shares (DL [10]; DD-012)**
The register is prima facie evidence only (Corporations Act s 176). Run our own ASIC and PPSR searches, review the constitution and any shareholders' agreement, confirm no options, convertibles, pre-emptive rights or encumbrances, and require delivery at Completion of share certificates (or lost-certificate indemnity), executed transfers, board approval of registration and resignations. The title warranty must be unqualified and outside disclosure.

**16. Lesser items**
- *Office lease (DD-007):* confirm the notification is given pre-Completion and that failure does not trigger a landlord termination right; make it a Completion deliverable.
- *Mossvale (DD-009):* a share sale generally isn't an assignment, but obtain the actual clause and check for a change-of-control provision; seek a written comfort letter if the contract is material.
- *DL [1.4] (no admission):* standard and acceptable, but it cuts both ways – the Seller cannot then rely on these disclosures as characterising matters as immaterial.

---

## C. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

| # | Issue | Position to take |
|---|-------|------------------|
| 1 | "All limitations apply to all Claims" | Reject; full carve-out list (fraud, fundamental, tax, indemnities, price adjustment, ACL, equitable relief) |
| 2 | Fundamental warranties under general caps | Reject; 100% cap, 6–7 yrs, no thresholds, no disclosure |
| 3 | Riverlark release post-Completion | Reject; repay at Completion from price, deed of release + PPSR discharge, indemnity |
| 4 | Bluefen consent | Hard CP, unconditional written consent, Buyer-satisfaction standard, no Seller waiver; price protection if conditions imposed |
| 5 | Bonuses omitted from funds flow | Deduct gross-up (incl. super/payroll tax) as Debt; itemise; indemnity |
| 6 | Ironquay | Payment + confirmatory assignment as CP; indemnity for loss of IP title, not just AUD 180k |
| 7 | Privacy incident | Finish assessment pre-Completion; notify if required; specific indemnity; no disclosure against warranties |
| 8 | General data-room/public-record disclosure | "Fairly disclosed" standard; listed searches only |
| 9 | Buyer knowledge cl 8.3 | Delete (fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals, excluding fundamental/tax/indemnities) |
| 10 | Cap / basket / time | Open at 50% tiered; tipping basket; related-claim aggregation; tax 7 yrs; escrow or W&I if Seller holds at 20% |
| 11 | Tax & IP regime | Separate caps/periods and tax indemnity |
| 12 | Sandbar, lease, Mossvale, title | Diligence follow-ups; treat uncommitted/unaccrued items as Debt; own title verification |

**Recommended tactical framing:** respond that the Buyer will accept a conventional general-warranty regime (cap/basket/18 months) *only* on the basis that it is confined to general commercial warranties, and that the five known issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006) are resolved through conditions precedent, price mechanics and specific indemnities rather than left to the warranty package. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter supports that framing.

*This memorandum is for the deal team's internal use and should be confirmed against the full SPA draft and current data-room index before the mark-up is issued.*
=== END ADVICE ===
